figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: one equation a = -ω²x played out across springs, pendulums, energy and resonance
figures.read: every result is ω=√(k/m), an energy share, or a resonance peak

figures.title: The phase ladder: v leads x, a leads v
figures.why: the three sinusoids differ only by quarter-turns
figures.data: x=A sin ωt; v leads by 90°; a opposite to x
figures.read: velocity a quarter-cycle ahead of displacement; acceleration points back at equilibrium

figures.title: Energy exchange: all kinetic in the middle, all potential at the ends
figures.why: the two shares trade without changing the total
figures.read: the box holds a fixed total poured between spring and motion

figures.title: Springs: parallel adds, series reciprocates
figures.why: the only work is finding k_eff before the period formula
figures.read: parallel is the recipe for stiffer, series for softer

figures.title: Resonance: small damping, tall sharp peak
figures.why: every forced-oscillator question is about the peak's height and width
figures.data: peak near ω=ω0; Q=ω0/2γ sets height and width
figures.read: light damping makes a needle-sharp spike; heavy damping flattens it

figures.title: Triage - route by the keyword
figures.why: the keyword names the route before any number is touched
figures.read: period wants system constants, initial conditions want the phase, speed wants energy

drawings.title: SHM sinusoidal waveform: x, v and a
drawings.show: three panels. Top: $x(t)=A\sin\omega t$. Middle: $v(t)=A\omega\cos\omega t$ (leads $x$ by $90°$). Bottom: $a(t)=-A\omega^2\sin\omega t$ (leads $v$ by $90°$, opposite to $x$). Mark the phase relationships.
drawings.search: "SHM displacement velocity acceleration phase relationship graph"

drawings.title: The SHM phasor diagram
drawings.show: a circle of radius $A$. A phasor (radius) rotates at angular speed $\omega$. The projection on the vertical axis is $x$. The velocity $v$ is the projection of a phasor of length $A\omega$ (rotated $90°$ ahead). The acceleration $a$ is the projection of a phasor of length $A\omega^2$ (rotated $180°$ from $x$, i.e., antiparallel).
drawings.search: "SHM phasor diagram circle projection velocity acceleration"

drawings.title: Energy versus displacement in SHM
drawings.show: $U=\frac{1}{2}kx^2$ (parabola), $K=\frac{1}{2}k(A^2-x^2)$ (inverted parabola), $E=$ constant (horizontal line). At $x=\pm A$: $U=E$, $K=0$. At $x=0$: $U=0$, $K=E$. The energies exchange at every instant.
drawings.search: "energy versus displacement simple harmonic motion kinetic potential graph"

drawings.title: Series and parallel spring configurations
drawings.show: left: two springs in series (one after the other, same force, displacements add). Right: two springs in parallel (side by side, same displacement, forces add). The effective spring constants shown.
drawings.search: "springs in series parallel effective spring constant diagram"

drawings.title: Simple pendulum with restoring-force decomposition
drawings.show: a pendulum at angle $\theta$ from vertical. The weight $mg$ resolved into: a component along the arc ($-mg\sin\theta$) and a component along the string (tension minus $mg\cos\theta$). For small $\theta$: $\sin\theta\approx\theta$, so the restoring "force" along the arc is $-mg\theta=-mgx/L=-kx$ with $k=mg/L$.
drawings.search: "simple pendulum restoring force small angle approximation diagram"

drawings.title: Lissajous figures for common frequency ratios
drawings.show: a $3\times3$ grid of Lissajous figures. Rows: $\omega_y/\omega_x=1,2,3$. Columns: phase difference $\delta=0,\pi/4,\pi/2$. The figures range from straight lines (1:1, $\delta=0$) to circles (1:1, $\delta=\pi/2$) to figure-eights (2:1, $\delta=\pi/4$) to complex curves (3:1).
drawings.search: "Lissajous figures frequency ratio phase difference grid"

drawings.title: Resonance curve: amplitude versus driving frequency
drawings.show: $A(\omega)$ vs $\omega/\omega_0$ for three values of damping $\gamma$: small (sharp peak), medium, and large (broad, low peak). The peak shifts slightly below $\omega_0$ for larger $\gamma$. The $Q$-factor $=\omega_0/(2\gamma)$ indicated.
drawings.search: "resonance amplitude versus driving frequency damping curves graph"

drawings.title: The two normal modes of coupled pendulums
drawings.show: left: in-phase mode — both pendulums displaced the same way, spring relaxed. Right: out-of-phase mode — pendulums displaced oppositely, spring stretched/compressed. The frequencies labelled.
drawings.search: "coupled pendulums normal modes in-phase out-of-phase diagram"

drawings.title: The SHM velocity–displacement ellipse and its area
drawings.show: a plot of $v$ vs $x$. The trajectory is an ellipse with semi-axes $A$ (on the $x$-axis) and $A\omega$ (on the $v$-axis). Each point on the ellipse represents a state of the oscillator. Its area in $x$–$v$ coordinates is $\pi A(A\omega)=\pi A^2\omega=2\pi E/(m\omega)$. In canonical $x$–$p$ phase space, $p=mv$ and the ellipse area is $2\pi E/\omega$. Ensure the two areas are not conflated.
drawings.search: "SHM phase space ellipse velocity displacement energy conservation"

drawings.title: The ballistic pendulum: collision then swing
drawings.show: three phases: (1) a bullet of mass $m$ at speed $v$ approaching a block of mass $M$ on a string of length $L$; (2) the bullet embeds — angular momentum conserved about the pivot; (3) the block+bullet system swings up to height $h$ — energy conserved.
drawings.search: "ballistic pendulum collision swing angular momentum energy conservation diagram"

drawings.title: The nonlinear pendulum: period versus amplitude
drawings.show: a graph of $T/T_0$ vs $\theta_0$ (the release angle). $T/T_0=1$ for small $\theta_0$, then increases gradually. At $\theta_0=90°$, $T/T_0\approx1.18$. At $\theta_0=170°$, $T/T_0\approx3$.
drawings.search: "pendulum period versus amplitude nonlinear correction graph"

drawings.title: The torsion pendulum
drawings.show: a wire suspending a disk. The disk is twisted by a small angle. The wire provides a restoring torque proportional to the twist angle. The disk oscillates with a period determined by the torsion constant and the moment of inertia about the wire axis.
